\frontchapter{Abstract}
JHQ-GPU studies how to execute JHQ's compressed primary/residual search efficiently within GPU memory. For fixed computed primary scores, grouped retention, merging and witnessed shared bounds preserve global top-$c$ selection under the stated ordering and memory-access conditions. Cartesian splitting replaces 256 LUT entries with $16+16$, giving a storage ratio $32/256=1/8$ with the same real-arithmetic score. Calibration compares sampled top-$k$ IDs with a larger-budget reference, without GT or a learned predictor.

On six RTX 5090 datasets, two-group LUTs lead in 22/24 cells; the largest index holds 17.78 million vectors at 20.44\,GiB resident memory. Full-pool calibration meets a $10^{-3}$ held-out
recall-loss target relative to the best tested budget in 12/12 cells, with
maximum loss 0.0006; smaller samples expose workload-dependent quality risk.
At recall 0.97 and batch 1,000, JHQ leads in three of four datasets and is
near parity with IVF-RaBitQ on arXiv. OpenAI runs use TF32; FP32 checks
retain favourable comparisons under a TF32-trained cache. At batch 8 and
the same recall, CAGRA fp32 leads on all four datasets. These results
locate the execution, quality and capacity trade-offs of GPU JHQ.

changes.after:
Vector search returns nearby embeddings from a large database. GPU
parallelism can accelerate distance calculations, but raw high-dimensional
vectors can exceed device memory. Compression makes larger indexes
resident; its benefit then depends on how codes are read, candidates are
selected and survivors are refined. This thesis asks how JHQ's compact
hierarchy can become an efficient GPU search system while keeping those
operations correct and measuring the resulting quality--speed trade-off.

CAGRA navigates a graph; compressed IVF scans chosen lists \cite{cagra,johnson_gpu,ivfrabitq}. Stella shows why compact storage matters (\cref{sec:7-7}):
\[
 S_{\rm raw}=67.81\,\mathrm{GiB}
 >S_{\rm GPU}=\frac{32607}{1024}\,\mathrm{GiB}
 >S_{\rm resident}=20.44\,\mathrm{GiB}.
\]

JHQ screens with primary codes and refines survivors with residuals \cite{jhq}. We vary execution and survivor count on the same trained index, measuring recall, speed, memory and construction cost, including losses.

GPU search can parallelise across queries, candidates and coordinates.
Warps have 32 threads with bounded block resources \cite{cuda_programming_guide}.
JHQ's broad primary scan and narrower residual refinement expose
different amounts of work. More blocks can improve utilisation for small
query batches, but duplicate tables, local state and merging add work.
Scheduling must account for both available parallelism and this overhead.

Faiss uses warp selection \cite{johnson_gpu}; bitonic/radix/merge choices trade state for work, alongside global selectors AIR/GridSelect \cite{gpu_topk}.

SONG parallelises graph search \cite{song}; CAGRA adjusts connectivity/search width \cite{cagra}. We compare fp32 and quantised CAGRA.

BANG uses host graphs to extend capacity \cite{bang}; JHQ retains compressed residency.
changes.after:
HNSW uses a hierarchy of proximity graphs to guide search from coarse
navigation to finer neighbourhoods \cite{hnsw}. GPU graph search must
also expose enough parallel work during traversal: SONG parallelises
graph search \cite{song}, while CAGRA adjusts connectivity and search
width \cite{cagra}. CAGRA's GPU-resident search makes it the graph
comparator here; both fp32 and quantised configurations are included.

DiskANN combines a graph index with SSD storage to search databases
larger than main memory \cite{diskann}. BANG uses host graphs to extend
GPU search capacity \cite{bang}. These systems move data across a
storage boundary; JHQ instead keeps its compressed hierarchy on the GPU.
The present comparison therefore tests resident execution rather than
SSD-backed search.

Historical CPU JHQ runs use different index parameters and recall/timing
protocols from E1 (\cref{sec:7-1}). Their throughput cannot establish a
matched-quality CPU/GPU speedup; that comparison remains unmeasured.

Evidence covers one GPU, six prepared datasets and squared-L2 top-10 (\cref{sec:7-smallbatch}). Near duplicates may remain; relevance labels are absent. Updates, concurrency, drift, service latency, billion-scale and multi-device use are untested.

changes.after:
向量检索从大型数据库中返回距离查询较近的嵌入向量。GPU 并行计算可以加速距离计算，但原始高维向量可能超出设备显存。压缩使更大的索引能够常驻 GPU；收益随后取决于编码读取、候选选择和精排的执行方式。本文研究如何将 JHQ 的紧凑层级表示实现为高效 GPU 搜索系统，同时保持这些操作的正确性，并测量质量与速度之间的权衡。

CAGRA 通过图进行导航，压缩 IVF 则扫描选定的倒排列表 \cite{cagra,johnson_gpu,ivfrabitq}。Stella 说明了紧凑存储为何重要（\cref{sec:7-7}）：
\[
 S_{\rm raw}=67.81\,\mathrm{GiB}
 >S_{\rm GPU}=\frac{32607}{1024}\,\mathrm{GiB}
 >S_{\rm resident}=20.44\,\mathrm{GiB}.
\]

JHQ 用主码筛选候选，再以残差对保留下来的候选精排 \cite{jhq}。本文在同一训练索引上改变执行方式和保留候选数，测量召回率、速度、显存和构建成本，也如实报告退步的情况。

warp 包含 32 个线程，block 可用资源有限 \cite{cuda_programming_guide}。JHQ 分别沿候选和坐标并行扫描与精排；额外的 block 会复制状态。

Faiss 使用 warp 级选择 \cite{johnson_gpu}；bitonic、radix 和归并在状态与工作量之间权衡，另有 AIR／GridSelect 等全局选择器 \cite{gpu_topk}。
changes.after:
GPU 搜索可沿查询、候选和坐标三个方向并行。warp 包含 32 个线程，block 可用资源有限 \cite{cuda_programming_guide}。JHQ 的广泛主码扫描与较窄的残差精排暴露了不同规模的工作量。更多 block 可以提高小 batch 下的利用率，但也会增加查找表、局部状态的复制和归并工作。调度需要同时考虑可用并行度和这些开销。

Faiss 使用 warp 级选择 \cite{johnson_gpu}；bitonic、radix 和归并在状态与工作量之间权衡，另有 AIR／GridSelect 等全局选择器 \cite{gpu_topk}。

changes.before:
SONG 并行化图搜索 \cite{song}；CAGRA 调整连通性与搜索宽度 \cite{cagra}。本文比较 fp32 和量化 CAGRA。

BANG 借助主机图扩展容量 \cite{bang}；JHQ 则保持压缩索引常驻 GPU。
changes.after:
HNSW 利用分层邻近图，使搜索从粗粒度导航逐步进入更细的邻域 \cite{hnsw}。GPU 图搜索还需在遍历过程中暴露足够的并行工作：SONG 并行化图搜索 \cite{song}，CAGRA 则调整连通性与搜索宽度 \cite{cagra}。CAGRA 的 GPU 常驻搜索适合作为本文的图索引对手；测试包含 fp32 和量化配置。

DiskANN 将图索引与 SSD 存储结合，搜索超过主存容量的数据库 \cite{diskann}。BANG 借助主机图扩展 GPU 搜索容量 \cite{bang}。这些系统跨越了存储边界，而 JHQ 将压缩层级保持在 GPU 上。因此，本文比较的是常驻执行，而非 SSD 后备搜索。
